A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AnomSeer and retain corresponding methods, experiments, and appendices A–E. All 21 pages of v1 and 24 pages of v2 were readable, including equations, tables, figures, and appendix examples.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark evaluations, component ablations, hyperparameter sensitivity, reasoning analyses, and case studies.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds optimization comparisons, scaling analyses, multivariate evaluation, augmentation experiments, and classical TSAD comparisons.

M1.justification: Appendix D.4 introduces a multivariate input adaptation that renders variables as subplots within one image. V1 evaluated channels individually and discussed joint visual reasoning as future work. ExpCoT generation, TimerPO's objectives, orthogonal integration, and model architecture remain unchanged; the new inference pseudocode documents the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix D.4 and Table 7 extend evaluation to jointly represented multivariate synthetic and real-world series, substantially broadening the previously univariate setting. A dedicated short/boundary-anomaly evaluation also expands coverage of a failure condition already illustrated in v1. The original three benchmarks remain; the new multivariate datasets are not identified.

E2.justification: Table 8 newly evaluates FFT, Matrix Profile, gradient detection, voting ensemble, ARIMA, and thresholding against AnomSeer. Table 6 adds PCGrad-style projection and cosine/CLIP-style alignment alternatives. The original Table 1 comparator set is unchanged, and the weighted-sum comparison repeats v1's existing no-orthogonalization ablation.

E3.justification: New experimental designs include training-data scaling from 1k to 5k examples, gradient-projection and alignment controls, an InfoNCE temperature of 0.07, joint multivariate plotting, and original-versus-augmented boundary evaluation. These extend the evaluation design without revising the retained main experiment's 3,200 training examples or default configuration. Several new dataset and augmentation settings remain unspecified.

E4.justification: Figure 13 adds learning curves and data-scaling analysis. Table 6 tests advantage-level versus gradient-level projection and OT versus alternative alignment objectives; Table 7 adds targeted augmentation robustness analysis. The earlier component ablations, alpha sensitivity, reasoning-distribution analysis, and failure case are retained.

E5.justification: V1 already reports means and standard deviations over three runs. V2 additionally reports 95% confidence-interval half-widths over three seeds for TimeMaster-3B and AnomSeer-3B/7B in Table 5. This expands uncertainty reporting without establishing an increase in runs.

E6.justification: Table 1's entries and the original ablation scores are unchanged. New results include average F1 of 76.3 for PCGrad, 71.7 for cosine alignment, and 73.4 for CLIP-style alignment versus TimerPO's 79.3. Table 7 adds multivariate scores of 83.5/72.4 and boundary scores of 56.2 versus 75.8 with augmentation. Classical comparisons and scaling curves add further results, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: TimerPO's mathematical construction remains unchanged apart from notation and indexing cleanup. New Appendix C.3 spells out the standard affiliation metrics already used in v1; it provides explanatory definitions rather than introducing a different metric, substantive theoretical argument, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims: classical evidence guides fine-grained reasoning through ExpCoT and TimerPO, improving detection and localization over MLLM baselines. The added appendix evidence does not redefine these announced contributions, and the conclusion retains its multivariate-extension limitation.

C2.justification: The new appendix interprets OT geometry and advantage-level projection, predicts benefits from further data scaling, argues for practical deployment, and discusses multivariate applicability and augmentation for boundary failures. It also introduces an overstatement: D.5 claims superiority across all anomaly types, although Table 8 gives FFT and ARIMA higher frequency scores than either AnomSeer variant.

D1.justification: V2 adds an AnomSeer repository pointer, detailed metric definitions, and 3B computational measurements: 12.4 training hours on four RTX A6000 GPUs, approximately 7 GB inference memory, and 4.8 seconds per sample. It removes dated commercial API identifiers and several dataset, baseline, checkpoint, and framework URLs. Existing core hyperparameters and hardware descriptions remain.

R1.justification: Appendix E substantially expands positioning beyond LLM-based TSAD to optimal transport in RL/LLM alignment and multi-objective optimization. New citations and comparisons distinguish reasoning-token alignment from outcome alignment and advantage-space projection from PCGrad-style gradient surgery. The changed Kong citation title/year refers to the same arXiv work, not an additional reference.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. V2 makes local language and affiliation edits, adds acknowledgements and an impact statement, expands metric and inference explanations, and inserts appendix subsections with updated cross-references. The added experiments do not entail extensive rewriting of the existing narrative.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the single-column preprint main text with a two-column conference layout and extensively resizes and relocates existing displays. It adds Tables 5–8, the learning/scaling Figure 13, and an inference algorithm display. The earlier failure case is retained as Figure 14 rather than newly introduced.

improvement.justification: The new OT/projection ablations and classical comparisons address gaps in v1's empirical support; uncertainty reporting, compute measurements, and the project link also improve assessability. The gains are limited by underspecified multivariate and augmentation protocols, removed resource/API details, and overinterpretation: D.5 claims superiority on every anomaly type despite FFT scoring 65.9 versus AnomSeer-7B's 60.8 on frequency anomalies in Table 8.
